t: Each amount designated in this Act by the Congress for Overseas Contingency Operations/Global War on Terrorism pursuant to section 251(b)(2)(A)(ii) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 shall be available only if the President subsequently so designates all such amounts and transmits such designations to the Congress.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the President's designation and transmittal to Congress is a formal consultative procedure. Both the President and Congress are inside the federal government, so this is intra-governmental notification on appropriations, not participation. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, given a hearing, or granted a right to sue.
fable.s: shall be available only if the President subsequently so designates all such amounts and transmits such designations to the Congress

opus.w: The only actors here are Congress and the President, and both are inside the federal government. Sending designations to Congress is a communication between parts of the government, so it is not participation. Nothing in the section involves consulting outsiders, a comment period, a hearing, an advisory body or a right to sue.
opus.s: shall be available only if the President subsequently so designates all such amounts and transmits such designations to the Congress
opus.b: Someone might be tempted to call this participation because the President must make a designation and send it to Congress, which looks like a formal step before the funds become available. That reading fails because both the President and Congress are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company, member of the public or other outside party takes part.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes a procedural requirement for the President to transmit fund designations to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so this interaction is internal. There is no involvement of state governments, the public, or other outside entities in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: Each amount designated in this Act by the Congress for Overseas Contingency Operations/Global War on Terrorism pursuant to section 251(b)(2)(A)(ii) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 shall be available only if the President subsequently so designates all such amounts and transmits such designations to the Congress.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that transmitting designations to Congress is a form of consultation or coordination. However, Congress is inside the federal government, and this is a procedural requirement for the release of funds, not a mechanism for outside parties to participate in decision-making.
